title: National assessment logistics — a readiness checklist for principals
description: A practical, checklist-based guide for Kenyan senior school principals on preparing the logistics of national assessments — venue, materials, staffing and student readiness.
body:
National assessments carry significant administrative weight — for Grade 12 candidates in particular, every logistical detail matters, because an administrative error can affect a student's results through no fault of their own. Principals who build a structured readiness checklist, reviewed well ahead of the assessment period, avoid the last-minute scramble that creates unnecessary risk.

Candidate registration and documentation

  • All candidates registered correctly with accurate names matching official identification documents
  • Index numbers and candidate details verified against the examination body's records well ahead of the assessment date
  • Any candidates with special needs requiring accommodations have those arrangements confirmed and documented in advance
  • Fee clearance status confirmed for all candidates, resolved well before assessment dates to avoid last-minute disruption

Venue and facilities

  • Examination room seating arranged according to required spacing and candidate capacity
  • Adequate lighting, ventilation, and furniture confirmed for all examination venues
  • Clear signage directing candidates to their correct venue and seat
  • Backup arrangements in place for power outages, particularly relevant for any assessment components requiring electricity

Staffing and invigilation

  • Invigilators assigned, briefed on protocols, and confirmed as available for all assessment sessions
  • A designated centre manager or coordinator with clear overall responsibility for the assessment period
  • Backup invigilators identified in case of staff illness or unavailability on the day
  • Security arrangements for examination materials confirmed, including secure storage before and after each session

The most common preventable error: Candidate detail mismatches between school records and the examination body's registration — a misspelled name, wrong date of birth, or incorrect subject combination — cause avoidable complications that are far easier to correct weeks in advance than during or after the assessment period. Verify these details as early as possible.

Student preparedness

  • All candidates briefed clearly on reporting time, required materials, and prohibited items
  • A mock assessment or orientation session conducted so candidates are familiar with the format and environment they will face
  • Transport arrangements confirmed for day scholars to ensure punctual arrival
  • A clear, communicated plan for candidates who fall ill during the assessment period

Communicating with parents during the assessment period

A brief WhatsApp update to parents ahead of the assessment period — key dates, what the school has done to prepare, and practical guidance for supporting their child at home during this time — extends the school's preparation efforts into the home environment and reduces parent anxiety-driven enquiries during an already demanding period for staff.

Building in review time before the deadline

Completing this checklist with two to three weeks of buffer before the assessment period, rather than finalising arrangements in the final days, gives the school time to correct any issues discovered during final review — a much safer position than discovering a problem with no time left to fix it.
